subject: [PATCH 0/2] sched/numa: stop VMA scan filters from gating promotion

reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: Addressed a double-put bug in fuse_try_move_page() where the folio refcount drops to zero prematurely. Suggested adding an extra folio_get() before replace_page_cache_folio() to maintain the reference.

reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: Responded to Sashiko's concerns about the patch causing unneeded rescanning and potential issues with concurrent scanners. Provided additional context and explanations.
reviews.raw_body:
On Fri, Sep 04, 2026 at 02:20:06PM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> @@ -4302,7 +4316,7 @@ static void task_numa_work(struct callback_head *work)
>  		 * VMA can cause others to become "permanently unaccessed" if a scan
>  		 * cycle is consumed entirely by the large VMA.
>  		 */
> -		vma->numab_state->slow_only = false;
> +		vma->numab_state->slow_only = ro_file;
>  		if (!vma_pids_forced && !vma_is_accessed(mm, vma)) {
>  			if (!(sysctl_numa_balancing_mode &
>  			      NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING)) {

Sashiko thinks this causes unneeded rescanning, but I don't think it
does. The cursor prevents it from restarting, and when we loop back
around reset_ptenuma_scan() bumps the sequence.

It also had concerns about concurrent scanners and ptl lock contention,
but mm->numa_next_scan only admits one per scan period.

Either way on a rewalk the scan hits pte_protnone() and moves on.

~Gregory

reviews.author: Sashiko
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about the patch causing unneeded rescanning and potential issues with concurrent scanners. Provided specific examples and code snippets.

2026-09-04.patch_summary: The patch series aims to stop VMA scan filters from gating promotion in the Linux kernel's NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) implementation. Specifically, it addresses two issues: the per-VMA PID filter and read-only file mapping exclusion. The patches modify existing code to allow for more efficient promotion of pages between memory tiers.
